description: Found a Frankfurt Standard Bank safe deposit box rental contract and key among Haddin's belongings. Andrew carefully examined the device and obtained important clues.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Expecting these idiots to pull off something this big is like expecting pigs to fly."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Oh, sorry, that must be my description that's off. Their backers are old Nazis in new disguises. It's even highly likely that the leader of the Free Corps is one of them."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm... it's a bit complicated. This is the first I've heard of it. I think the House of Solomon might be of some help to your investigation. Many historians and people investigating Nazi crimes from that era have gone there to look up information."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Heh, that just happens to match my initial question. It seems you don't know any more relevant information either." He smiles somewhat helplessly. "But I wouldn't mind if the news that the Free Corps is backed by some Nazi remnants from Sachsenhausen reached the ears of other organizations."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Isn't this something you already know? The leaders of the Free Corps often visit him."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: @player2 "Is the internal strife related to the opera troupe and the pawnshop?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The Blake incident? No need to test me with something everyone knows."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I don't have any more questions. Thank you very much." He stands up after a simple expression of gratitude. "If we succeed, we'll expose the Free Corps and the old Nazi organization behind it down to their roots. Then you should have a chance to settle the score with them."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also stands up. "To our success?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm~" He neither confirms nor denies. "It's not time for that yet. By the way, you now have a choice before you."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Oh? What opportunity?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He doesn't clink glasses. Instead, he turns around, makes a phone call, and then hands the receiver to player5.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David puts down his glass and strokes his chin.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Takes the receiver. "Hello."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: A male voice comes from the other end of the line, low and calm: "Good afternoon, gentlemen, or ladies. This is the United States Central Intelligence Agency, Frankfurt Station."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Listen to see if the other party's accent is a pure, rustic Yankee drawl.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Such an elite naturally uses standard German.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So it's friends from the CIA. Good afternoon. What can we do for you?" The tone is relaxed and calm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The other party pauses, seemingly not expecting you to be so composed. Then, he says slowly: "We can offer you protection, even help clear up some trouble for you with MI6... Of course, provided you prove yourselves worthy of cooperation."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It seems our disguise was somewhat clumsy after all." He smiles self-deprecatingly. "What do you want?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We need two things." The voice on the phone is unhurried, as if reading from a list.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I need to discuss this with my companions. Could you provide a contact method? There's still time before the July 6th action, you probably aren't in a rush for these few hours, right?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not possible. If you want our help, you must follow our orders. If not? That's fine too, but it's best not to get in the way. Otherwise... you'll find yourselves on the opposite side as well."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Hangs up the phone.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After player5 hangs up, the boss also looks indifferent. "Just refused like that?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player2 "Haven't prepared myself mentally yet." Shrugs as if joking.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You've got guts. I wish you smooth sailing ahead!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thanks for the good wishes."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also leaves, his mind heavy with concerns.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The story record of the Algorithm of the Heart continues. Currently recorded text: 5684.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Leaving the Hermes Club, drive back to the previously agreed rendezvous point.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 and the other had a pleasant conversation with Hermes and learned that equipment can be purchased here, such as firearms, ammunition, vehicles, bombs, cameras, etc., as well as a safe house where one can sleep soundly.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: How much money do we have left? David calculates.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: How much does the safe house cost? If it's too expensive, player5 plans to use guns as collateral. "We're a bit tight on cash lately, do you accept barter? I can offer a submachine gun."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Two." He states cleanly and decisively that there's no room for negotiation.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Two for one night? I could earn more than that by robbing with these two guns in one night." Laughs angrily at the exorbitant demand. "One."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No discussion. We don't have many safe bases left in Frankfurt either; this was originally prepared for making a comeback. Besides, you don't have much choice."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright, you win." Pouts, helplessly raises both hands, then hands over the goods to the boss. "Here, top-quality new guns. Give me the safe house address and key."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David feels regretful about those two guns in his heart, his gaze lingering reluctantly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Just for tonight. Remember to clean up when you leave tomorrow, and throw the key into a sewer."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "OK."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The safe house is located in the northern suburbs of Frankfurt, near the university district.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: There's no time to lose; hurry back to meet up with the accomplices. We've obtained a lot of information here that needs to be shared.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Can you throw in a set of fake license plates?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Then Hermes provides you with a fake license plate.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The after-sales service is not bad; David feels slightly comforted.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: So Gray and the other left the Wonder Room first and went to the newspaper office, until four o'clock when David and the other drove to the agreed location.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David gets out of the car, filled with a bellyful of intelligence, intending to share it with Gray and Andrew. Let Gray and Andrew get in the car; we'll talk inside, guys.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Is the newspaper office really a safe place? Andrew is full of suspicion, locked in a hard-to-notice corner, looking around, especially watching the entrance.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Call Andrew to get in the car, eager to share our Wonder Room experience.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Get in the car; the car is the best, and we can run if we want, as long as we're not blocked by a heavy truck.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "God, did things go smoothly on your end? We went to find Hermes; Rabin almost offered a knee."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thankfully, God favored us."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It was smooth at first, but then it became more and more outrageous... In short, things developed far beyond our imagination, involving many incomprehensible things." Andrew pours out everything about the consciousness test experiment and the Wonder Tool, and also shares the possession hypothesis.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also shares his side's intelligence with his accomplices. "What, soul transfer? Can one person's soul really be stuffed into another body? And what about magic, did you see it with your own eyes?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There's such a thing?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It was poured directly into my mind in a wondrous way... You might not believe it, but I still feel a bit dreamy about it."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: While sharing the intelligence, they are greatly shocked.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison describes the general appearance of the shop she saw. "And this way, some things start to make sense."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I don't know, I don't know anything. That woman said that." "I'm very afraid of her! I don't even know what that was."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "For example, that old man's body might contain the soul of an old Nazi, and the original owner of this device seems to be exactly the Heim that Haddin is looking for."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Sadly, after all this, I'm no longer surprised by anything unreal—even though the training manual never mentioned it."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "...Indeed. Then we have reason to believe the old man frequently visited by the leader of the Free Corps might be some kind of soul vessel."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should we check out the second floor of the Guvich Clinic tonight? I'm a bit curious about what's there."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "According to Haddin's records, that leader has also been missing for a long time; perhaps he also used this device to hide in someone else's body."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "I think it's very necessary."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Another point is about Haddin. The Americans seem to know no less than we do, and they want Haddin dead—but that might not help us return to MI6. Their so-called reward is still just a blank check, while a living Haddin is clearly more valuable to us."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We already have a dead Haddin."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If he goes back, he'll only meet his end, and that's already been confirmed by us, hasn't it?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Should we first follow Guvich's records to capture some 'heartless ones,' then lock Haddin inside..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "At the very least, I don't think we should harm an innocent person."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David fell silent. Andrew's question was quite sharp, making it difficult for him to answer immediately.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If it really comes to it, we could always transfer him into someone else," he shrugged. "Or stuff him into me?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If I were from the organization, I'd probably suspect you were acting out multiple personality disorder."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Uh, I think all this is a bit beyond my ability to accept. I'd rather imagine a living Haddin being with us..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That makes sense. So we'd better find a suitable person to stuff him into. What do you think about some lucky neo-Nazi kid or one of the Nazi leaders present?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Actually, I think Brandt would be just fine."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Agreed."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sigh... Despite encountering so many miraculous things, without a living Haddin we still have a hard time proving ourselves. Maybe we need to prove that station chief is problematic." Alison shook her head.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This magic is really exciting..." He snapped his fingers excitedly after hearing David's suggestion. "David, you're a fucking genius!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew, curled up in his seat, uttered a faint voice, "But wouldn't that mean letting a spy occupy a high position..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "But I think that guy wouldn't appear in the same place as Haddin."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Now I don't doubt whether Haddin can really travel through time; there have been too many bizarre things."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We need to protect him from the CIA and the Academy."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What's our next move? The clinic is best visited at night when no one's around."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "If that boss can stuff a soul into a little doll, then maybe we can also stash Haddin somewhere first and stuff him into Brandt when we meet him." David began his fantasy time. "As for the clinic, we'll find out when we explore it tonight."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So we need to get to the place where Haddin plans to act early tomorrow and make contact with him."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "She said it's best not to exceed a hundred times a day," Alison shrugged.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If this thing is really so convenient and without side effects, theoretically we could knock someone out and stuff everyone we encounter into them."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "God, player5, you're a genius."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "But I haven't used it yet, and I don't know exactly how it works."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I suggest we assume this thing can only be used once for now."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew remained silent in the back seat. His understanding of his colleagues had been updated.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If we find it can still be used, that would be a pleasant surprise."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I wonder if it can be implanted into an animal."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "But animals can't talk; we haven't heard of monkeys talking yet. Parrots can, but where would we find one?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Can it even be stuffed into this?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I'm wondering if we can stuff all the neo-Nazis into parrots when we scout their lair tomorrow morning—if we get discovered."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Speaking of which, we encountered people from the Free Corps at the auction house; they also wanted this thing and said price was no object."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We've discovered their weapon applications..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Good thing we acted quickly."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Indeed, if they got their hands on this thing, we'd have no chance of turning things around."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Makes sense. Where's that safe house they mentioned?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Near the university district. Let's go."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Let's go."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Grab some dinner on the way.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: We should eat something good for this meal; there aren't many left!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After eating pork knuckle, you head to the safe house. This place has the typical characteristics of a university district: a one-bedroom designed for renting to poor students.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Obviously, the lady gets the bed; the three guys sleep on the floor.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's nothing in the room except a mattress, forcing you to buy several used blankets discarded by college students from a second-hand market.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Sigh, still have to rely on ourselves. Hope the poor students' blankets don't have lice.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Hope the weather isn't too cold!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: It's July; Andrew actually woke up a few times from the heat. The place is简陋, but at least there are no bedbugs, so you all slept relatively soundly until waking up late at night.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Get up, slap your face to wake up, check your gear, confirm lockpicking tools and weapons are on you.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Prepare for action! Andrew tightens his clothes, though he's not particularly skilled at this.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Time to get to work, gentlemen."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Alright, guys, let's go when you're ready."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Equip all pistols with silencers, bring flashlights.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Silencers attached, small flashlights in hand, the guys park the car in an alley near the clinic and take a city walk.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Swap the car's license plates back to the original ones, wait for everyone to gather, then drive.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We could also consider roughing it in the car later, if we still need to sleep."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Get some gloves and hoods for everyone to wear.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: We're all outlaws.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We can only stay here for one night."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew gets dressed according to the instructions.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, I'll clean up the traces. You guys check if there's anything we missed."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Tonight is the night of the desperadoes.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Head out to work.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You head to the psychology clinic, reaching the door under the cover of night.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Observe at the door to see if any light is leaking out, then press a cup against it to listen for any movement.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David looks around, keeping watch for his accomplices in the dead of night.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: It's pitch black inside, and no sound comes from within.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Assist in preparing to pick the lock.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Take out lockpicking tools, feel the structure of the lock, and try to open it.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Mountains and soil listen to your wishes. Regardless of karma and retribution, fate now slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray picks the door lock open with a wire.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: All things are impermanent, fate is uncertain, the answer is known only to a few.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player5 .ra Spot Hidden

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Rolled by <player2> on behalf:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 discovers a trigger-type alarm device not far from the door. If you had opened the door and entered recklessly, you would have definitely triggered this thing, and then attracting the patrolling officer on duty would have been a huge trouble.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Can this thing be disarmed?" David asks the real expert.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Looks like we need to be careful from now on."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let me see how to disarm it or disable it." Try to use your professional knowledge and skills to deal with this thing.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite good at many things.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 disarms the alarm's trigger device; now it's blind.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Well done."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We really have experts in various fields among us."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite good at many things.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Next, Andrew moves carefully inside the house, worried there might be other small devices here.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Quietly and quickly move inside with a small flashlight, leaving the door slightly ajar to restore its original state.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I think it's necessary."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "The lookout definitely can't stay outside. Since we're all in the clinic, we might as well all go upstairs together."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Leave one person on the first floor to keep an eye on the situation outside? So we don't get surrounded without knowing it."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "That makes sense."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then I'll be the lookout. But loitering around the building is even more suspicious. I'll keep watch from upstairs instead."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison shines her flashlight around the first floor as she passes by to see if there are any obvious changes compared to when she came in the afternoon.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: No obvious changes.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Then, watch your step and go upstairs to explore the unknown area.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: The second floor, our target is the second floor! And the second floor definitely has tighter security measures. Andrew isn't concerned about being discovered for trespassing later anymore; there is no 'later' now.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Tiptoe quietly upstairs and observe the layout of the rooms on the second floor.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You grip your weapons, adjust your breathing, muffle your footsteps, and push open the door to the second floor—

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew starts examining this bedroom with a burglar's mindset, ready to play his part thoroughly.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The carpet is soft and clean, the curtains are half-drawn, the bed is neatly made with a dust cover over it, looks like no one has lived here for a while.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then David slips into the bathroom to see if there's a safe or something, though it's unlikely.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Search the room for anything like a notebook that might record experimental data.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Naturally, there's nothing like that in the bedroom. It seems the room's owner doesn't like bringing work into rest time.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Pace back and forth near the windows to keep watch.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Looks like we're looking in the wrong direction." Alison decides to go to the first floor to see if Gurevich's office has any of these things.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Where did he hide the money and the data? Could they still be on the first floor?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 You push, but the door doesn't budge; it seems to be locked.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Examine the layout of the rooms on the second floor. Considering the building size seen from outside, are these two rooms the only ones that fit its architectural design?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh?" There's a lock here too. Alison takes out her lockpicking tools again, trying to open this lock as well, while cautiously checking if there's any electronic alarm or mechanism like the one in Haddin's room behind this door.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The cycle of fate is like shackles, and will you now gamble on the path with no trace to follow?

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew assists from the side.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: That's reasonable, since the first floor wasn't very big to begin with.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David doesn't find anything and goes down to help as well.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The filing cabinet has a transparent glass window but is locked. You can see the lock is intact, not broken or picked.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Looks like this is the main event." Alison first checks if there are any trigger mechanisms in the room.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player6>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Seems that way." David also searches the room for any mechanisms.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Obviously, there are no alarm measures inside; the door lock is the only guardian angel here.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David presses close to the filing cabinet glass, reading the labels on the files through the glass.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Take action! Let the colleagues check the desk first. Alison, see what's going on with this safe.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Start rummaging through the "property"—especially the documents.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player3 The box labeled "Algorithm of the Heart Research Samples" containing samples No. 1～100.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player3>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David returns defeated and starts rummaging through the desk with Andrew.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: While keeping watch, move over to David's side to take a look.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s Spot Hidden check result:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Samples of the Algorithm of the Heart... a hundred of them, so many."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Didn't understand, honestly goes back outside to keep watch.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What was the hit rate for the draw again?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The lock on an ordinary file cabinet... without a doubt.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Then directly attempt to pick the lock.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Locksmith check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: It's filled with manila document boxes. You notice that the sample boxes for NO.37, 42, and 73 are not among them.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: What's needed here is the burglar effect. So, where's the money?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We're actually too late; this safe has already been ransacked by someone."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: On the desk, a letter from Standard Bank's safe deposit box service, informing that the safe deposit box jointly held with Andreas Rilke has been opened, and confirming that the items entrusted by Professor Govich for storage have been properly placed.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Damn it all."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then who are the corresponding labels for these three people?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Ugh, he really is connected with Rilke."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's also a letter from Solomon House, thanking Dr. Govich for volunteering as a psychological counselor last November and asking if he has any updates regarding Mr. Grove's whereabouts.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "37, 42, 73... Does that mean three people have transferred their souls?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player4 "Then those are probably the three anomalous samples identified by the Algorithm of the Heart."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: So where's the money?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Andrew, are there any keys or similar things on the desk over there?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Under the desk, there's a drawer that appears to be locked.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Let me look, nothing much so far..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison goes to work with her lockpicking tools.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player4>'s Locksmith check result:
